title: The Masque of the Red Death
focus: the futile attempt to shut out death

teacherSummary.text: While a plague called the Red Death kills a third of his realm, Prince Prospero walls himself and a thousand nobles inside a fortified abbey. He throws a masked ball in seven colored rooms running east to west, the last black with blood-red windows and a great ebony clock. At midnight a guest disguised as a Red Death corpse appears; Prospero chases him into the black room and dies, and the revelers find the costume empty. The Red Death has entered, and all die.

My answer: Prospero's attitude that the external world could take care of itself tells us he thinks wealth and walls can shut out death; his indifference to suffering is the arrogance the story will punish.
